children: Aixtron could experience weaker growth after 2027 if demand for its products takes a hit from a potential slowdown in the buildout of artificial-intelligence infrastructure, UBS analysts write in a research note. They downgrade their rating on the stock to sell from neutral and cut their target price to 24 euros from 50 euros. The German group, an equipment provider to the semiconductor industry, has benefited from AI demand in recent years, and analysts expect Aixtron to deliver an exceptionally strong 2027, citing a substantial buildout of laser capacity for AI data-center optical networking and incremental demand from AI-related power semiconductors. However, they say they expect laser capacity expansion to slow in 2028. Aixtron shares trade 10% lower at 28.85 euros. (mauro.orru@wsj.com)
